title: Agile Inverse Design Framework for mmWave Devices | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: Agile Inverse Design Framework for mmWave Devices | EECS at UC Berkeley Agile Inverse Design Framework for mmWave Devices Yueting Li EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/ December 1, 2025 This project report presents a versatile and computationally efficient inverse design (InvDes) framework for RF and millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated circuits. In contrast to neural network based approaches that require extensive training and large datasets, the proposed methodology employs a lumped RLGC circuit representation for pixel modeling, enabling ultra-fast circuit-level simulations. A physics-guided genetic algorithm (GA) combined with an analytical screening mechanism eliminates non-viable candidates and accelerates convergence by orders of magnitude. The framework achieves complete design closure from initialization to layout generation within minutes and is inherently portable across technology nodes and frequency bands without retraining. The proposed methodology is validated through silicon implementations of bandpass filters, power dividers, and power amplifiers fabricated in 28-nm and 65-nm CMOS technologies. Measured results show close agreement with simulations, demonstrating the frameworkâs robustness, flexibility, and accuracy in synthesizing complex pixelated structures with grid sizes up to 91 Ã 91 and pixel widths as small as 4 Î¼m. The framework offers a generalizable and high-throughput solution for the rapid inverse design of mmWave circuits.
